Plans have been submitted to turn a historic outbuilding beside a Grade I listed building into a five-bedroom home. Mick Hilless has applied to Huntingdonshire District Council to turn a barn and office building linked to Bodsey House into a home on Bodsey Toll Road, Ramsey. Bodsey House is Grade I listed, meaning it is of exceptional interest. The property was once a 13th-century hermitage belonging to Ramsey Abbey but has since been altered and turned into a family home. The plans would turn the barn and office building at the rear of the site into one five-bedroom home. The historic barn is curtilage listed, which means it is legally protected as it sits within the grounds of a listed building. Documents by Scroxton Architects say the barn and office building are dilapidated and no longer suitable for modern agricultural or commercial use. The plans would demolish the modern open-sided portal barn at the rear and replace it with a two-storey extension forming a five-bedroom home. The site is about 1.8km north-east of Ramsey and covers 0.2 hectares. rawItems.title: Cambs High Sheriff praises hospice charity for its ‘exceptional care’
rawItems.content: A hospice in Milton has been praised for its "exceptional care" by the High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire during a recent visit. Francis Burkitt DL, High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire, visited East Anglia’s Children’s Hospices (EACH) in Milton to present certificates of appreciation to long-serving staff and volunteers. He was joined by his wife Jo and Jonathan Jelley MBE JP during the visit, which included a tour of the care floor and meetings with children, families, and staff. Francis said: "I was delighted to be given the chance to celebrate and thank some of those who do so much to support EACH’s work. The High Sheriff of Cambridgeshire visited EACH’s hospice in Milton (Image: EACH) "EACH is widely known and highly regarded as one of the very best organisations in our county, doing so much for children and families across Cambridgeshire. "It’s the people who help deliver that exceptional care and support, and I can’t speak highly enough of the wonderful staff who work here." He also recognised the vital role of volunteers, adding: "Likewise, the amazing volunteers who selflessly give their time. "That’s why I was so thrilled to honour and recognise the contribution made by people like Mick and Graham here at Milton." High Sheriff’s Certificates of Appreciation were awarded to staff members Sandra Holmes, Helen Thrower and Sallyann Parkin, as well as volunteers Mick Housden and Graham Shipley. Awards were presented to staff and volunteers during the visit (Image: EACH) Additional

rawItems.title: Cambridgeshire firefighting family responds together to major Holme Fen wildfire
rawItems.content: Firefighting runs in the family for a Cambridgeshire crew. Alex Gould recently became an on-call firefighter at Thorney Fire Station, where she works alongside her long-serving father, Phil. She said: "Responding alongside my dad at Thorney has been so much fun. "Growing up, Dad had always been in the fire service, so being able to experience my first shout alongside him was a unique experience. "I'm very lucky to be able to learn from him and the others at Thorney who have been incredibly welcoming. "My first working job was made even better by the fact that Emily was the one to mobilise us." Emily is Alex’s sister, but they are not the only Goulds serving the fire service. Phil’s brother, Anthony Gould, is chief fire officer at Peterborough Volunteer Fire Brigade, while Anthony’s son, Jacob, is a wholetime firefighter with the service. The family showed that dedication by helping tackle the Holme Fen wildfire, one of the county’s biggest incidents in years. Every Gould currently serving with the service helped respond to the major incident, either on the frontline or behind the scenes in control. The service hopes the Goulds’ story will inspire others to become firefighters. Inspired to become the first firefighter in your family—or join relatives already in the role? Visit our careers section to find out how you can help your community. rawItems.title: Ban for drink driver after THREE times the limit wall crash
rawItems.content: A drink driver has been banned from the road after crashing into a wall while more than three times the legal limit. The 46-year-old man from Ramsey was more than three times the legal alcohol limit when he crashed a red Mazda in Malthouse Close, Huntingdon, on July 25. He blew 138 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath at the roadside, compared to the legal limit of 35. At Peterborough Magistrates' Court on September 23, he was disqualified from driving for 26 months and must also carry out 80 hours of unpaid work

rawItems.title: New dig to start at Cambridgeshire Bronze Age site with £700,000 of funding
rawItems.content: Archaeologists will begin a new dig at one of Britain’s most important Bronze Age sites in Cambridgeshire next year. The dig, at Flag Fen near Peterborough, must begin before information preserved in peat is lost as the ground dries out amid climate change. The timber causeway at the site was 1.1 km long, about 20 metres wide, and had about 22,000 posts, Mark Knight of Cambridge Archaeological Unit said. It was thought to have played a role in communication and trade, connecting two pieces of dry land over an area that got wet around 3,300 years ago, he said. Mr Knight, who will be excavation director on the new dig, said information was preserved in wet peat without oxygen for thousands of years but the hotter climate is drying the peat out. He said that a section of the causeway that was “a bit closer to the surface” is “drying out a little bit quicker”. “If we don’t excavate it in the next couple of years it will be gone forever so we will lose all of that information,” he said. Jacqui Mooney, general manager at Flag Fen Archaeology Park, said she was also concerned by a peatland fire that broke out at Holme Fen, around 11 miles from Flag Fen, during drought conditions last month. items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Amenities Committee (Agenda Full Council 10 September 2026): Approved £14,500 contract for drainage improvements across Spinningfield recreation ground, alongside installation of replacement inclusive swing sets in September.

items.title: Great Whyte Pedestrian Safety & Speed Limit Review
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Minutes (Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan Examiner Report August 2026): Council resolved to submit a formal request to Cambridgeshire County Council Highways for a 20mph speed zone and upgraded zebra crossing along Great Whyte, following resident traffic survey feedback.

items.title: Planning Committee Recommends Refusal for 25 Dwellings Off Oilmills Road
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Planning Minutes (Planning Meeting Minutes 27 August 2026): Unanimously recommended refusal for outline application 26/00142/OUT on grounds of highway safety on Oilmills Road, surface water flood risk, and overdevelopment beyond the settlement boundary.

items.title: Planning Committee Approves High Street Commercial Refurbishment & Signage
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Planning Minutes (Planning Meeting Minutes 27 August 2026): Supported planning application 26/00188/FUL for commercial shopfront renovation and heritage signage in the Ramsey Conservation Area.
